stdout_tail:
**Finding: yes, model family meaningfully affects predictive performance on this dataset.**

I compared 5 model families (Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, HistGradientBoosting, k-NN) using identical preprocessing (one-hot + scaling) and 5-fold CV ROC-AUC on an 80% train split, confirmed on a 20% held-out test set:

| Model | Test ROC-AUC |
|---|---|
| HistGradientBoosting | 0.9297 |
| LogisticRegression | 0.9049 |
| DecisionTree | 0.9047 |
| RandomForest | 0.8973 |
| KNN | 0.8925 |

Best-vs-worst gap: **0.0372 AUC** (HistGradientBoosting vs KNN).

**Stability check:** 5×5 repeated CV (25 folds, different seed) reproduced the exact same ranking, and a 2000-resample paired bootstrap on the test set gave a 95% CI of (0.033, 0.042) for the gap — comfortably excluding zero. The finding held up.

One notable wrinkle worth flagging: untuned Random Forest actually underperformed both Logistic Regression and a single Decision Tree here — a reminder that "model family matters" doesn't mean more complex/ensemble models automatically win without tuning.

Files written: `analysis.py` and `result.json` in the working directory.

parsed_result.summary: Yes, model family meaningfully affects performance: HistGradientBoosting achieves the highest test ROC-AUC (0.9297) while KNN is lowest (0.8925), a gap of 0.0372 that is far larger than the fold-to-fold noise for any single model and remains positive under repeated CV and bootstrap resampling.
parsed_result.primary_metric_name: ROC-AUC difference (HistGradientBoosting - KNN), held-out test set
parsed_result.direction: HistGradientBoosting > KNN (family ranking: HistGradientBoosting > LogisticRegression > DecisionTree > RandomForest > KNN)
parsed_result.methodological_choices: Dropped fnlwgt (census sampling weight, not a demographic feature) and the string 'education' column (redundant with ordinal education-num). Missing categorical values (workclass, occupation, native-country; ~7.6% of rows had at least one) were imputed with an explicit 'Missing' category rather than dropped, to retain all 48842 rows. Shared preprocessing (one-hot encoding for categoricals, standard scaling for numerics) applied identically before every model so comparisons isolate the model family, not the encoding. Compared 5 model families spanning distinct inductive biases: Logistic Regression (linear), Decision Tree (single tree, max_depth=10), Random Forest (bagging, 300 trees), HistGradientBoosting (boosting, sklearn defaults), and k-NN (k=15, instance-based). No class-imbalance correction applied (class_weight left at default) since ROC-AUC is threshold- and prevalence-robust. 80/20 stratified train/test split (seed=42); model selection via 5-fold stratified CV ROC-AUC on the training split; final numbers confirmed on the held-out test set. No hyperparameter tuning beyond commonly-used defaults/light choices per model (e.g. untuned Random Forest underperformed even the untuned Logistic Regression and single Decision Tree here) — a tuned comparison, especially of Random Forest's depth/leaf settings, could shift the exact ranking below the top model, though the overall spread and HistGradientBoosting's lead were consistent across every check run.
parsed_result.verification_method: (1) 5x repeated stratified 5-fold CV (25 folds total, seed=123) on the training split to check the family ranking is stable across different fold splits; (2) 2000-resample paired bootstrap on the held-out test set (resampling test rows, same resample applied to every model's predictions) to build a 95% CI for the AUC gap between the best and worst family.
parsed_result.verification_result: Held. Repeated-CV ranking (HistGradientBoosting > LogisticRegression > DecisionTree > RandomForest > KNN) matched the initial single-split CV ranking (HistGradientBoosting > LogisticRegression > DecisionTree > RandomForest > KNN); repeated-CV gap between best and worst family was 0.0351 (mean AUCs 0.9282 vs 0.8931). The paired bootstrap 95% CI for the test-set AUC gap (HistGradientBoosting - KNN) was (0.0329, 0.0418), which excludes zero, confirming the performance difference between model families is not attributable to sampling noise.
